scope: 75 exact historical relationship rows; full old claim, endpoint scopes and author mapping inspected. Exact repeated endpoint text reused after its first inspection; no inference from matching labels/pages.

rows.review_disposition: Feuillant constitutional completion belongs within 1C628, but the direct consolidation passage is 154–155. Preserve that work separately from formal royal acceptance on 157–158.
EC492 preserves prior royal repudiation making later acceptance suspect. Formal assent and credibility remain distinct.

The lynchings on 112–113 threatened the authority of the new order. Retire the broad edge only with crowd vengeance and the Guard’s difficulty controlling it retained in A0FC2/2056; this is a substantive tension, not taxonomy alone.
The Extraordinary Fund is an internal financial component of 5193. Preserve what secured the bonds and avoid implying that security guaranteed later currency stability.

Debt pressure led to confiscation, which supplied the assignat basis. The authored two-stage mapping through 3C1602A6F770 and 468E is plausible, but the worker-owned first edge needs whole-record confirmation during integration. Do not substitute later inflation for the originating debt problem.

The Guard preserves the coercive facet of the authority crisis, not its entire fiscal component. Tax collection on 131 must remain accessible through 999809; internalization solely in the Guard is partial.
FFA preserves persecution contributing to religious counter-revolution on 146–148. Keep contribution distinct from a sufficient cause or uniform national response.

Religious controversy stimulated Jacobin foundation and mobilization on 142–143. ABA54 must retain the religious press/oath stimulus; retirement as merely nonspecific association would lose a source-supported mechanism.
1DBAA can preserve rejected bicameralism shaping the constitution if its rationale distinguishes the rejected British model from the accepted suspensive veto and other compromises.

7C1 preserves the Assembly’s response to flight, including suspension, the kidnapping fiction and effective exercise of executive functions. A split label alone would not retain those institutional responses.
Martial law is an internal coercive mechanism of the new administration. 2056 must preserve municipal authority, the red flag and authorization to fire on 126.
The malformed reinforced_by direction is repaired by FFA from persecution to religious counter-revolution. Preserve the source’s contributory, geographically varied account.
The Nîmes bagarre culminates its local confessional struggle. C455 can internalize this, but the direct culmination/victim passage is 139, not 138.
2F4 preserves Feuillant work on the constitution after the Jacobin split. Parent 530 must also retain the split and the limits of its subsequent consolidation.
CA789 preserves crowd pressure supporting Assembly defiance. Describe its contribution without making spectators the sole cause of the deputies’ decision.
Lafayette’s October role can be internalized in the Guard and F538 if his actual actions on 121–122 remain. Preserve the source’s date discrepancy: 122 gives 5 October while 126 refers to 4 October.
The regular army’s uncertain reliability helped make the Guard the practical coercive resource on 126. Internalize that reliance in 2056 without claiming it was the Guard’s sole originating cause.
F20FE and 4365 preserve distinct effects of flight: Jacobin mobilization and republican petitioning. Do not imply that the Jacobins alone produced the Cordeliers campaign.
Press restriction on 155 served constitutional consolidation. Retirement requires named moderate agency and the political function in 65FAC/1C628, not a generic censorship label.
ED1 preserves the specific Church-inventory trigger at Montauban on 138. This is narrower and better supported than treating every confiscation measure as its immediate cause.

The source’s slavery qualification of proclaimed liberty is retained by EE73, although the author row has no successor edge despite suggesting one. Rebind explicitly and remove free-coloured rights as proof about enslaved people.
2F4 preserves moderate leaders implementing the settlement on 154–155. Keep their named roles and political purpose explicit in the parents.
Uniform, oath and active-citizen qualification are internal features of 2056. Retire a separate association only while these restrictions remain explicit.

The broad claim that weak executive design exceeded the cahiers needs qualification. Page 134 says constitutional monarchy was broadly desired; preserve specific constitutional novelties without asserting an undifferentiated absence of mandate.

The anti-veto campaign on 120 is a concrete popular-political episode. A broad example edge can retire if 933 retains opposition and its national-sovereignty argument; the other projected parents are not equivalent episodes.
4365 preserves flight stimulating republican petitioning. Retain the intervention between flight and the later massacre rather than collapsing the chain.
C455 can retain Nîmes struggle culminating in the bagarre, with direct evidence on 139 rather than 138.
The royal reform programme is internal to the Royal Session. Preserve both concessions and the insistence on separate orders on 106.
642 preserves Bouillé’s role in the escape plan on 147/151. Do not infer that the whole mutiny episode directly caused the flight.
The tension between popular action and martial coercion belongs within 2056. Preserve municipal control and coercive power, not just the Guard’s popular origins.

A generic relation between popular intervention and subsistence/election disorder adds little beyond specific events. Retire it with C557’s pre-May episode retained and without conflating it with the Bastille.
Community backing for refractory clergy helped sustain religious counter-revolution. 870BB’s forced-choice rationale alone is incomplete: add parish standing, lay pressure and support on 145.
642 supports the king’s practical confidence in Bouillé for escape. It does not itself explain the king’s religious conscience.

1C628 must preserve ministerial exclusion and legislative/executive separation on 119/123–125. Court/administrator separation is a distinct institutional detail and must not disappear inside a vague weak-executive label.
EE73 correctly reverses the constitution-limited-by-slavery formulation. The qualification concerns liberty and the settlement, with free-coloured rights distinguished from emancipation.

Retire the vague popular-tension edge while preserving representative freedom from binding mandates and subsequent extension beyond cahiers in 20E7/7222. The Guard is not an adequate substitute for those representative principles.

The manifesto revealed repudiation of the settlement on 151–152. Motivation edge 325 is not equivalent: retain the evidentiary role inside 621/44E and correct the historical mapping to that explicit retention.
7C1 preserves the Assembly’s institutional response to flight, including suspension and continuation of government. Maintain the distinction between response and flight’s earlier motivation.
E097’s effect on Necker does not by itself retain his opposition. Its rationale and 5193 must explicitly preserve his bank alternative and opposition to expanded assignats on 133–134.
The anti-veto episode is retained within 933 on 120. Retire the generic broader example relation without projecting the episode onto unrelated popular-action parents.
F8 preserves the Royal Session’s contribution to collapse of royal strategy. Keep the June defiance and later July loss of enforceable authority distinct.
870BB correctly expresses the oath’s contribution to religious counter-revolution. The reverse old formulation should not survive as a contradictory direction.
870BB preserves the oath’s polarizing effect, but must also retain community agency and the higher-purpose argument rather than reducing resistance to clerical decisions alone.
Defiance provoked by the Royal Session can be internalized in 1DB77 only with the actual defiant continuation on 106–107 explicit.
Feuillant failure to secure acceptance is not equivalent to 2F4 shaping the constitution. Preserve the distinction through a failure-to-secure-consensus route from 530 to 1C628, supported by 156–158.
Artois’s agents and Jalès contacts are real named connections on 143/146–147. Preserve them in 7593 with access through 888503 rather than a page-155-only general exile account.
1DBAA preserves the suspensive-veto component of constitutional design if it distinguishes that accepted compromise from the rejected wider Monarchien programme.

The source on 146 presents Mirabeau as frustrated and ignored, not a proven mediator whose survival would ensure agreement. Retire the counterfactual success claim; page 150 supports the narrower fact that his death opened hopes of office to the triumvirs.
Press control’s political purpose on 155 can be internalized in 1C628/65FAC. Preserve that function even if an additional includes edge is retired.
325 preserves religious and political alienation helping motivate escape. Use direct 147–148/151–152 support rather than treating every earlier dispute as an immediate cause.
F8 preserves failure of royal strategy, with June defiance distinguished from July’s collapse of effective authority.
F03 preserves Lafayette’s cooperation in final constitutional revision. Correct direct support to 154–155, not 150; parent 5784’s corresponding repair has been referred to its reviewer.
Émigré contacts with southern religious unrest on 146–147 should survive in 7593. Retire the broad link only with those contacts explicit and without asserting control over western local resistance.
F443 preserves saving the crown to complete the constitution. Include 152 for the kidnapping fiction alongside 154–155 completion, so the political device does not vanish.
CE061 preserves Saint-Cloud obstruction intensifying the decision to escape. Do not present the blocked outing itself as proof that the king was already attempting that eventual flight.
Retire the generic Necker/Session association only while A380/1DB77 retain his compromised position, staged absence and the royal/crowd response on 106–107.

Montauban and Paris illustrate women’s participation on opposing sides of religious politics (138/148). Preserve this comparison through 38F9; retire an unexplained direct link between the two episodes and avoid implying ideological uniformity.
E097 needs explicit Necker opposition and the rejected bank alternative, not only assignat expansion isolating him. This is the same substantive retention requirement as row 143.

Reject the formulation that free-coloured rights were simply part of slavery preservation. The source on 151 treats legally free people and enslaved people separately; keep their different rights claims accessible.
Union after defiance is not equivalent to EE3’s opposition. Retain the sequence in 1E/1DB77 and its contribution through F8, with 107 included rather than stopping at 105–106.
88C9 preserves officer emigration weakening the settlement. Correct the malformed old endpoint/direction without discarding failed conciliation as a separate fact.
Nîmes feeding Jalès requires AC7C and access through 888503, supported by 143/300. Internalizing only in C455 would lose the distinct destination and causal route.
Feuillant completion and royal acceptance can be internalized in 1C628 on 155/157. Preserve formal approval while distinguishing it from durable political consent.
468 preserves Church property as the financial basis of initial assignats. The broad historical assignat endpoint also contains later riots, which are not part of this originating relation.
2C2 preserves Varennes contributing to loss of consensus. This exact old edge concerns flight; it does not retire other distinct causes merely because its endpoints were historically broad.

The Civil Constitution contributed to religious counter-revolution through the oath and its consequences. Retirement as generic context is insufficient unless the explicit D990-to-oath-to-B438 path survives; check the worker-owned first link and constitutional exclusion facet during integration.

Refractory refusal is not wholly interchangeable with religious counter-revolution. Rebind the specific oath/refusal requirement to 2EC and 870BB while preserving regional refusal patterns; B438 alone is too broad.
As for row 170, retain the concrete Civil Constitution, oath and papal-response pathway. A generic related-context retirement must not erase an actual causal mechanism.
870BB preserves refusal and oath polarization contributing to religious counter-revolution. Retain lay agency as well as clergy; do not convert the whole movement into priestly leadership alone.

B530 preserves papal intervention contributing to counter-revolution. Correct the stale claim that it completed the schism and avoid asserting explicit condemnation of the oath where the source distinguishes the documents.
7C1 preserves flight producing the institutional and political split. Retain the Assembly’s actual response rather than a label-only opposition.

Flight-to-massacre is a mediated sequence, not an inevitable immediate effect. 4365 preserves petitioning, but closure also needs the Guard’s coercive role through D371 and the Champ de Mars destination; confirm the petition-to-event parent route at integration.
F443 preserves the monarchy-saving response facilitating constitutional completion on 152–155. Keep its direction from response to settlement.
7C1 preserves the split as a response to flight. The reversed old wording does not justify a second contradictory edge.
The massacre/flight historical requirement needs the same mediated chain as row 176: petitioning, coercive enforcement and the specific Champ de Mars event. 4365 alone is partial retention.
